thread:
maria: heads up — since the 03:10 deploy I'm seeing intermittent packet drops between GPU nodes in us-west-2 (east-west). Training jobs hit gRPC stalls and some pods restart. 5-10% of p99 RPCs failing for a short window. :thinking:
jamal: can you paste the pod/node names and a quick graph? do we have tcp retransmits or just application-level timeouts?
olivia: grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/encap-p95?panel=13 shows a spike at 03:12 for vxlan tunnels (us-west2-gpu-pool). p99 latency jumps and retransmits on node-to-node flows.
maria: pod: ml-train-22, nodes: gpu-usw2-047, gpu-usw2-059. attaching a short tcpdump from gpu-usw2-047 (captured on vxlan0):
```
11:03:12.123456 IP 10.10.4.7.7345 > 10.10.6.9.52345: Flags [P.], seq 123:567, ack 98, win 29200, length 444
11:03:12.123789 IP 10.10.6.9.52345 > 10.10.4.7.7345: Flags [.], ack 567, win 28900, length 0
11:03:12.223111 IP 10.10.4.7.7345 > 10.10.6.9.52345: Flags [P.], seq 567:900, ack 98, win 29200, length 333
11:03:12.323999 IP 10.10.6.9.52345 > 10.10.4.7.7345: Flags [R.], seq 900, ack 0, win 0, length 0
```
jamal: RSTs on the return path? that's odd. do we see any encapsulation errors on the nodes or underlay drops?
lee: correlating with node patching logs — a partial kernel ABI bump rolled out to the west GPU pool at 02:55 (driver + NIC firmware updates). could be offload interaction with vxlan.
olivia: sysctl and ethtool quick checks from gpu-usw2-047:
```
ethtool -k eth0 shows: gso: on, gro: on, tso: on
ip link show vxlan0 mtu 1450
ss -ti dst 10.10.6.9:52345 shows some retransmits and 'acked' gaps
```
maria: tried tcpdump on the physical NIC and vxlan at the same time — saw the packet forwarded out on eth0 but the vxlan side didn't always deliver to the container. suggests an offload/GRO reassembly edge.
jamal: try disabling GSO/GRO on vxlan0 and see if the window improves for 10-15 minutes? low-risk rollback. command: `sudo ethtool -K vxlan0 gso off gro off tso off`
lee: note — doing that will increase CPU on the node for large flows. but it's a good canary.
maria: applied on gpu-usw2-047 and 059. immediate change: p99 RTT drops back to baseline, no RSTs observed in the next 2 cycles. :thumbsup: 
jamal: good quick win. still need to know root cause — offload interaction with the new NIC firmware or kernel handling of fragmented UDP/encap. please collect `dmesg` and `ethtool -S` for the nodes.
olivia: opening a diagnostics ticket and capturing ethtool stats, dmesg, and a continuous tcpdump for 30m. putting nodes in maintenance window and scheduling canary across 3 more nodes.
sre-oncall: monitoring-bot reported 03:18: alert cleared — encap retransmit spike subsided after gso/gro toggle. tagging infra-networking and kernel teams.
monitoring-bot: [ALERT] encap-tx-retransmit-rate spike cleared (rule: encap.retransmit.usw2). linked runbook: https://confluence.internal/encap-triage
lee: long-term options: revert kernel/firmware bump to the previous release for west pool, or patch our eBPF handling of vxlan GRO. also consider setting default vxlan MTU to 1400 for headroom.
jamal: let's do this plan: 1) roll the GSO/GRO change to the rest of the canary nodes (non-prod) 2) collect kernel oops/dmesg and open a follow-up with NIC vendor 3) schedule a controlled rollback of the 02:55 kernel bump if vendor can't reproduce quickly. I'll create a jira: INFRA-6421.
maria: adding notes to the incident doc with commands and quick workaround steps. thanks all.
jamal: one more ask — add a perf counter comparison (cpu sys% and net interrupts) before/after disabling GSO so we can quantify cost. we should estimate the extra core impact for scaled training.
lee: noted. I'll run perf counters and share.
maria: closing the thread for now — will re-open if the canary nodes show regressions after wider rollout. :eyes:
